paragraphs.text: [Liu An basket tea](liu-an:definition) is a [dark tea](dark:definition) from Anhui, a leaf left to change slowly after it is made. Despite the name, it is made in [Qimen County](anhui:places-inside) in the south of the province rather than in the city of Lu'an, from the same small-leaf bush that gives Keemun. Its making ends with steps of its own: the fired leaf is spread outdoors for one [night of dew](liu-an:making), steamed soft and packed into bamboo baskets lined with leaf, then rested for years before it is sold.

This leaf dates from 1990. Making had stopped in the 1930s and 1940s, when war cut the [southern trade](liu-an:southern-trade) to Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macau. It came back after tea people from Hong Kong sent an aged basket to Anhui in 1983 and asked for it to be made again, and commercial making returned in the early 1990s, so this tea comes from the first years of that return. At thirty-six years it has had the long keeping the style is [made for](liu-an:ageing).

brewing.text: Use water at or near the boil, rinse the leaf quickly, and keep the steeps short, each a little longer than the last, in a gaiwan or clay pot; doses run from about 3 to 8 grams for 100 ml, for six to ten or more steeps. A small piece of the basket's bamboo leaf is often brewed with it. Aged tea can also be simmered in a larger pot, about 1 gram to 200 to 300 ml, for a few minutes or longer.

notice.text: A redder, browner liquor, the smoke gone, and the cup moving toward medicinal, woody and camphor notes, often with betel nut.
